A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A*-Thought work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, compression and training-time measurements, ablations, and reasoning examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds non-mathematical evaluations, smaller-model experiments, test-time sampling results, and additional ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the stated BIS inputs from complete-trajectory pairs to individual-step pairs. However, Equation 4 already conditions on individual steps in v1 and remains unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. The PDFs leave uncertain whether this changes the scoring procedure or corrects its description.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates four mathematical benchmarks. v2 adds LiveCodeBench and MMLU evaluations in Table 2 and ARC in the beta sensitivity study, substantially extending evaluation beyond the original mathematical coverage. The original training data and mathematical benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding original experiments retain CoD, both BtC variants, TokenSkip, and the same backbone and fine-tuning controls. Added experiments use already represented comparison methods; the smaller-model study evaluates TokenSkip in additional model configurations.

E3.justification: New protocols include best-of-N sampling with N=8 and pass@1/2/4/8 reporting, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 14B-Instruct configurations, verification-depth comparisons at kmin=5 and 15, and beta values of 0.1, 0.5, and 0.9. These extend the evaluation design; the original training settings and default hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds verification-depth and current-cost-weight ablations, transfer tests from mathematical training to non-mathematical tasks, model-size comparisons, and a test-time-scaling compatibility study. These examine substantial additional questions beyond v1's retained BIS, alpha, kmax, training-loss, and case analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The eight candidate generations in v2's sampling experiment constitute an inference protocol, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original numerical tables and plotted results are retained. New Tables 2, 3, 5, 6, and 9 add substantial results, including LiveCodeBench accuracy of 39.0% for A*-Thought versus 12.0% for QwQ-32B at 4096 tokens, and 72.0% average mathematical accuracy with kmin=15. The latter is an additional setting, not a replacement for the retained 69.3% result at kmin=5.

T1.justification: The BIS, attention, likelihood, and search-cost equations remain unchanged. No new assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are introduced. The scoring-input wording correction does not change the existing Equation 4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims about bidirectional scoring, A* compression, efficiency, and generalizability. Additional experiments expand their supporting evidence without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly interprets non-mathematical performance as transfer of a learned reasoning pattern, and Appendix B argues compatibility with test-time scaling. Section 4.2 shifts its summary from highest ACU to highest efficiency and accuracy, although retained tables still show high-budget accuracy tradeoffs. The SFT-only limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 corrects the scoring-input description and specifies supplementary model identities, sampling count, and ablation settings. Existing optimizer settings, hardware, training-time measurements, prompts, and code/data access information are retained. Detailed benchmark splits and sampling parameters are not supplied for the additions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged. References move across pages, but there is no substantive revision to novelty positioning or relationships to prior methods.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, removes a duplicated sentence, adds analysis subsections and appendix sections, and includes funding acknowledgments and a conference footer. Most existing exposition remains verbatim; the document is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated tables for out-of-domain performance, verification depth, test-time scaling, smaller models, and beta sensitivity. It moves v1 Figure 7 into the main text as Figure 5 and places the two retained backbone-result tables together on one appendix page. Existing plotted data are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added transfer and smaller-model evaluations strengthen evidence beyond v1's mathematical tests on 32B models, while the new ablations clarify accuracy–compression tradeoffs. The gain is tempered by brief protocol documentation and the out-of-domain comparison's omission of the fine-tuned control used in Table 1. These additions provide useful but incompletely controlled support for broader applicability.
